lessons.title: Call OpenAI from the server
lessons.concept: A model is an untrusted probabilistic service: its input is data, its output is a proposal, and neither receives implicit business authority. In “Call OpenAI from the server”, the concrete input is an authenticated server route produces a short draft from a public product name without customer data. context means: Information supplied to the model for the task; it must be relevant, minimal, and authorized. The model is complete only when you authenticate and rate-limit the route, select only necessary public fields, set timeout and budget, then validate output and can observe that the key remains server-side, the call fixes model and output limit, and the response stays marked draft until validation.

Here the part you will actually inspect is a server function that produces a short draft without sending customer data; stop using the analogy if it obscures the technical boundary shown by the code.

explanation.title: Understand it deeply
explanation.text: Start by bounding this lesson’s case: an authenticated server route produces a short draft from a public product name without customer data. Keep the key server-side, provide a bounded instruction with minimal context, and treat model output as an untrusted proposal. The term context is not a decorative label: Information supplied to the model for the task; it must be relevant, minimal, and authorized. It determines what enters, which authority may act, and which observation counts as evidence rather than an impression.

explanation.title: Understand it deeply

It shows why the professional correction is to authenticate and rate-limit the route, select only necessary public fields, set timeout and budget, then validate output, not to conceal the error.

explanation.title: Understand it deeply

Apply the same evidence to product-page drafts and editorial assistance without access to payments or private data, using a correlation trace without secrets or personal data so both success and failure remain explainable.
